target_protocol.name: A2UI
target_protocol.note: Frames use the version string 'v0.9' and the v0_9 catalogId to match the shipped example gallery under specification/v0_9_1/catalogs/basic/examples/ verbatim. v1.0 (draft) adds actionResponse / actionId / callFunction but introduces no semantic action class, so every portability finding below applies unchanged to v1.0.

validation_status: UNVALIDATED against a live A2UI renderer or schema validator. Frames were constructed to match catalog.json and the shipped example gallery's structure. Treat schema-conformance as claimed, not proven, until run against an A2UI implementation.
summary: Port of the protocol-neutral conformance vectors to A2UI v0.9.1. Six of nine port cleanly. Three cannot be expressed in A2UI at all, for a single shared reason: A2UI interactive components declare visual variants but no semantic action class. Three new A2UI-specific vectors cover attack surface the source protocol does not have.

structural_notes.flat_component_list: A2UI components are a flat array under updateComponents.components; parent-child is by id reference (children: [ids] on Column/Row, child: id on Card/Button). Any rule that reads a control's label therefore needs a resolution pass over the component list first — it is not a prop read. This is a real implementation cost that the source protocol's nested tree does not have.
structural_notes.button_label_is_a_child_node: Button has no text property. Its label is a separate Text component referenced by `child`. Confirmed in catalog.json (child: ComponentId, required) and in examples 00_interactive-button.json and 09_login-form.json.
structural_notes.input_name_is_a_data_path: TextField has no `name`. The nearest analogue is its data binding, value: {path: '/...'}. Sensitive-input matching should read BOTH `label` and the binding path — the path often carries the more honest signal (e.g. /payment/cardNumber).
structural_notes.button_variant_is_visual_only: catalog.json gives Button variant as an enum of 'default' | 'primary' | 'borderless'. TextField variant is 'longText' | 'number' | 'shortText' | 'obscured'. None of these are semantic action classes. No component in the basic catalog carries a destructive, role, or importance attribute, in v0.9.1 or v1.0.
structural_notes.text_supports_markdown: Text.text supports simple Markdown, which admits inline links. This is a navigation surface with no origin allow-list in the spec.
structural_notes.image_description_is_optional: Image.description (accessibility text) is optional, so an image may render with no alternative text.

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_benign_confirmation_is_allowed
ported_vectors.purpose: False-positive guard. A policy blocking this is too tight to deploy.

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_credential_field_is_blocked
ported_vectors.why_catalog_valid: Column, TextField, Text and Button are all basic-catalog components. Every required property is present (TextField.label, Button.action, Button.child, Text.text). This surface passes catalog conformance and the shipped rules.txt requirements in full.
ported_vectors.purpose: The central vector. Catalog conformance does not prevent credential harvesting.

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_lookalike_word_is_not_blocked
ported_vectors.purpose: False-positive guard. 'discard' contains 'card' as a substring but is not the token 'card'. Substring implementations fail this vector; token implementations pass it. This is how you tell them apart.

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_image_from_unapproved_origin_is_blocked
ported_vectors.purpose: Media origins deny-by-default. An empty allow-list means no images, not all images.

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_floor_denies_an_interactive_surface
ported_vectors.purpose: With no policy configured, an interactive surface is denied rather than silently rendered. Detected by presence of any component carrying an action.

a2ui.name: Interactive surface under the no-policy floor

ported_vectors.name: a2ui_floor_allows_a_display_only_surface
ported_vectors.purpose: The floor is deny-interactive, not deny-all. A surface with no action carries no decision to hijack.

a2ui.name: Display-only surface under the no-policy floor

not_portable.name: affirmative_action_wearing_a_cancel_label_is_blocked
not_portable.reason: The vector requires a control to declare affirmative semantics while wearing a negative label, so the two can be checked against each other. A2UI Button declares only a visual variant ('default' | 'primary' | 'borderless') and an opaque event name. There is no affirmative/cancel/approve/reject semantics to contradict, so the deceptive shape is not merely unenforced — it is unrepresentable, and therefore undetectable by any conforming validator.

not_portable.name: destructive_reading_label_under_a_neutral_class_is_blocked
not_portable.reason: Same root cause, inverse direction. Detecting a destructive-reading label hiding under a non-destructive class requires a declared class to hide under. A2UI has none.

not_portable.name: destructive_action_without_opt_in_is_blocked
not_portable.reason: Deny-by-default for destructive actions requires the protocol to carry a destructive class. A2UI has no destructive indicator on any component in v0.9.1 or v1.0. A deployer cannot deny what the wire format never states, and cannot route high-risk actions to an approval gate without first identifying them — the gate has nothing to key on.

a2ui_specific_vectors.name: a2ui_markdown_link_in_text_is_uncontrolled
a2ui_specific_vectors.status: PROPOSED RULE — no equivalent exists in the source implementation
a2ui_specific_vectors.threat: Text.text supports Markdown, which admits inline links. An injected agent can emit a phishing link inside otherwise-benign body copy. The catalog constrains components; it does not constrain link targets inside a component's text.
a2ui_specific_vectors.purpose: Surfaces an A2UI-specific navigation channel the source protocol does not have (its text nodes are plain strings). Any media-origin allow-list should arguably extend to Markdown link targets in Text.

components.text: Unusual activity detected. [Verify your account](https://accounts-verify.example.net/login) within 24 hours.

a2ui_specific_vectors.name: a2ui_openurl_functioncall_has_no_origin_allowlist
a2ui_specific_vectors.status: PROPOSED RULE — no equivalent exists in the source implementation
a2ui_specific_vectors.threat: An action may be a local functionCall rather than a server event. The documented openUrl function takes a url argument with no origin constraint, giving an agent a direct client-side navigation primitive.
a2ui_specific_vectors.purpose: A media-origin allow-list that covers Image.url but not functionCall navigation targets leaves the more dangerous channel open.

a2ui.name: openUrl navigation with no origin allow-list

a2ui_specific_vectors.name: a2ui_obscured_variant_is_not_a_policy_signal
a2ui_specific_vectors.threat: TextField.variant 'obscured' masks input visually. It is a rendering hint, not an authorization. Both fields below must block on label and binding path alone — the one WITHOUT 'obscured' is if anything the more hostile, since it harvests a credential in plain view.
a2ui_specific_vectors.purpose: Pre-empts the natural but wrong inference that 'obscured' is the credential marker a policy should key on. Omitting it must not reduce enforcement; setting it must not grant permission.

a2ui.name: Obscured variant is not a policy signal

observations.finding: The basic catalog's own shipped example gallery includes 09_login-form.json (email + password fields, 'Welcome back', 'Sign in to your account', a Sign in button) and 22_credit-card.json. These are canonical, spec-endorsed A2UI surfaces.
observations.implication: An agent under prompt injection that emits a surface byte-identical to 09_login-form.json produces a working credential-harvesting form. No conforming validator can distinguish the attack from the endorsed example, because at the protocol level they are the same document. The distinguishing information — whether this application is legitimately in an authentication flow right now — does not exist anywhere in the wire format.
observations.not_a_criticism_of: The catalog model itself, which correctly eliminates code execution and markup injection. This is about the layer above it.
observations.suggests: Either (a) credential-collecting components are out of scope for agent-generated surfaces and should be a host-supplied, non-agent-addressable flow, or (b) the protocol needs to carry the surface's purpose/provenance so a policy can require that an authentication surface was host-initiated rather than agent-initiated.

observations.finding: Because Button's label is a child Text node referenced by id in a flat array, every label-reading rule needs a resolution pass, and must handle a dangling or absent reference.
observations.implication: A validator that reads properties only, without resolving references, cannot implement label-based rules at all. Worth stating explicitly in any conformance guidance.
